name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Challenger Martha Fierro has raised only about $485 thousand with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances near 98%
model.rationale: Garcia holds a Houston-area seat that leans Democratic by 17 points, has the advantages of incumbency, and has outraised Fierro roughly two-to-one with over $560 thousand in outside support. Markets price her near 98%, and no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive race.
model.watch: A major red-wave national environment or unexpected outside spending against Garcia could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that voted Democratic by about 17 points in recent elections. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent, having raised nearly $1 million and drawn more than half a million dollars in outside support, while holding a cash advantage over her challenger.

Republican Martha Fierro has raised a modest sum and attracted no reported outside spending, leaving her with little visible infrastructure to contest a seat this favorable to Democrats. Prediction markets put Garcia's chances near 98%. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
